segment.source: <end>
Thanks for the help, and good luck. We're both gonna need it.<end>
Perhaps our paths will cross again, partner. Have a good one.<end>

::The air smells like gunpowder and burning, and the ringing in your ears has yet to subside. You glance back at the ramp you somehow managed to kick open - adrenaline does wonders for the human body - and there you see the dazed gunslinger shambling about.
He has trouble finding the exit as his goggles are flickering on and off.::<end>
::Turn around and help him.::<end>
::Get as far away from the railcar as possible.::<end>

::You approach the railcar and grab him by the coat. By a stroke of luck, the large metal crate inside proved to be a perfect cover, previously from a storm of lead, and now from the enemy's vision.::<end>

::Now in the clear, it takes him a moment to remove and reset his goggles. He looks back and sees the carnage.::
What... happened?<end>
::[Perception]:: They set up a firing position in the wall behind the railcar. Couldn't see how they looked and how many there are, but there was more than a few.<end>

::He looks at the railcar's charred, but not overly damaged wheels.::
EMP mine. Sons of rats. Couldn't tell left from right when it hit me.
I owe you.<end>
You'll get to repay me real soon. We got better chances of making it out if we work together. You with me?<end>

::He checks his energy pistol. Its power is low, but it's still functional.::
I'm in.<end>
Guess it's you and me against what sounded like a tonne of heavy ordnance... and a bunch of ratbags who sure know how to use it.<end>
I like those chances. Ready or not, here I come.<end>
Lead the way.<end>
<end>
Follow me.<end>
Follow me, and stop sneaking.<end>
Let's discuss tactics.<end>
Let's.<end>
<end>
Follow me closely.<end>
I'm right behind you.<end>
Follow me from a moderate distance.<end>
Sure. Lead the way.<end>
Follow me from a great distance.<end>
Got it. I'll give you all the space you need.<end>
When I start sneaking, you start sneaking.<end>
They won't know I exist.<end>
Don't sneak with me anymore.<end>
If you say so. Just don't get me into trouble.<end>
Turn on your shield when I do.<end>
Without delay.<end>
Stop turning your shield on when I do.<end>
No problem.<end>
Avoid engaging enemies.<end>
Very well. But I sure hope you know what you're doing.<end>
Engage enemies at will.<end>
I ain't got a problem with that.<end>
There's something else...<end>
I'm listening.<end>
That's all for now.<end>
About your gear...<end>
<end>
Move!<end>
We need to switch places.<end>
Let's do it fast and as least awkward as possible.<end>
::Switch places with him.::<end>
Not gonna happen. <end>
We're too far away.<end>
The stims - use 'em.<end>
Sneak.<end>
Stop sneaking.<end>
Turn your shield on.<end>
Turn your shield off.<end>
Wait for me here.<end>
Wait for me here - and stay out of sight.<end>
::[Disabled]:: A charon for your thoughts?<end>
<end>
I think we're done here. Let them sleep.<end>
We got him. Won't bring Nimble and the rest back, but we got him. I think we're done here.<end>
We've made it in.<end>
<end>
To think people in the past used to travel here carefree... Puts some things into perspective.<end>
I don't like this station. The sooner we leave the better.<end>
Rest stations. Spent some time in a Lower Underrail one many years ago. But I had far too expensive equipment to be able to truly rest.<end>
Feels good to be back.<end>
No thoughts. Just action.<end>
And we certainly aren't going to fight them head on. I have a plan...<end>
First we need to move. We're sitting hoppers here.<end>
To hell with this! I'm getting out of here, even if I have to walk back to South Underrail.<end>
That's all the help you're getting. I work alone. And we better split before whoever's out there gets to us.<end>

::He looks around where to go.::
Crap.<end>
Get moving, we're sitting hoppers here.<end>
Sorry, but that's just how I roll.<end>
::Leave.::<end>
We got ambushed, buddy. We got ambushed hard.<end>
Carnage, that's what it is.<end>
Get a hold of yourself, man. We got hostiles around us.<end>
Hey, partner. Heading north by any chance? Thought you might want some company.<end>
<end>
Ron. How'd you end up here?<end>
Pure coincidence, $(context.player.Name).<end>
Let's go. Hopefully it won't end up like the last time... ::[Ends the game]::<end>
Let's go. Hopefully it won't end up like the last time... ::[Ends the game with some important business left unfinished]::<end>
I got some things to wrap up here.<end>
My train departs soon, so I'd rather not linger.<end>
Perhaps our paths will cross again. Goodbye.<end>
North's not for me. This is where I belong.<end>
In that case, have a good one.<end>
<end>
::You walk up to him opening a cold brew. ::<end>
::As soon as he sees you, he motions Zilla::<end>

:: for another one to appear, then drops a few coins on the counter.::
Right on time, partner.<end>
This is certainly a lot more casual than dark territory. Not yet sure if it's safer.<end>
That is not an unfounded question.<end>
<end>
::She slides the bottle toward you.::<end>
Drink's on me.<end>
I don't think I know your name. You can call me, Ron.<end>
::[Intelligence]:: Is that short for Ronald or Aaron?<end>
It's Ronald. Westrock.<end>
$(context.player.Name). <end>
Cheers, $(context.player.Name). ::He raises his bottle.::<end>
To a long life!<end>

::You clink your drinkware audibly.::
Everywhere I show up, people have all these questions.<end>
I'm sure you do too.<end>
This time I won't be asking any. I'll just let you speak.<end>
Hm. Sure.<end>

::It takes him a few moments, each one used to look at a certain part of the station. The reflections is his goggles make it seem like each turn of his head is a trip to a different time of his life. Until...::<end>

About... ten years ago I used to work for a company in Dis, DETeK, a private directed-energy weapons contractor for North Underrail. Only a few years after Protectorate took over, and in the midst of Free Drones madness. Advanced weaponry business was lucrative at the time.<end>
DETek... Directed Energy Tech or Technologies.<end>

Technologies - yes; but the former part - yes and no. The company was owned by a husband and wife - Diane Emerson and David Englund, both names neatly fitting into the acronym. She was the weapons designer and the brains behind it all, but David was the wealthy short-tempered husband who made things happen by throwing dollars at it.<end>
So that's where you got that pistol.<end>
It's my former service pistol. <end>
Biometrically locked. I'm the only one who can use it.<end>
It was my job to protect Diane. I was young. She was charming.<end>
An affair? This is getting better and better.<end>
She was a mature woman. Older than me. Very intelligent and attractive, even at her most unattractive. And I was young. Things happened.<end>
So I'm guessing the husband found out eventually.<end>

There is more to it. Once the company began to grow, David also grew more voracious. The guy could have any woman, so why not ditch the old one and get a new one, or new ones. He had already found people who could take over her work.<end>

You see, I wasn't there to protect Diane from kidnappers or Free Drone saboteurs, but from her husband. I didn't know it at the time, but I must've known it instinctively, as I never liked the son of a rat. ::He takes another sip from the bottle.::<end>
It was Diane Emerson Technologies, and he wanted it to be David Englund Technologies. She had started the company before she married him. They had no children.<end>
So what happened next?<end>

I failed. I was supposed to protect her, but emotions made me lower my guard. She was shot dead, by a stream under the open doming cavern outside of Dis. We shouldn't have been there, but we wanted to be alone far from everyone. I was so... out of it I didn't even see the attacker until it was too late.<end>

According to the official story, Diane and I were plotting to kill David, but once we were found out I led her out of Dis and killed her, trying to cover up the whole thing. And they found my gun, or at least a pistol just like mine with the same user id. I know, the story's got more holes than a sieve, but dollars plug those holes surprisingly easy.<end>

And so I had no choice. Either risk death penalty, or try my luck here. The whole story I heard many years later; back then I just knew they were going to pin it on me, and that I had to disappear.<end>

Ten years have passed since. DETeK is no more. David got what he deserved eventually.
I was thinking about returning to North Underrail. That's why I took the job. Enter the region through the back door.<end>
Now, with the luck I had, I think it's time to let go of the past and go through the front entrance.<end>
::And with that, he takes out his energy pistol and puts it on the table.::<end>
Keep that thing holstered or I'm calling the enforcers.<end>
This'll take but a moment, hon.<end>
$(context.player.Name), hold it by the grip. Go ahead.<end>
Oh, yeah. ::Do as he says.::<end>

::The screen flashes:
Successfully added a new user:
*TSMSL2SR - $(context.player.Name)*::<end>
I'm letting go of the past. And that piece there, that's past.<end>
::He takes one final sip from his bottle and puts it back on the counter.::<end>
Now what?<end>
Now I leave. A few minor things left to do... and then I'm off.<end>
I should be going as well.<end>
I won't tell you to take care. You seem to be good at that already. Have a good one, $(context.player.Name).<end>
Take care, Ron.<end>
Goodbye then.<end>
::Say nothing and just do what he says.::<end>
Keep it. You're going to need it still.<end>
::He looks at it, and quietly puts it back in the holster.::<end>
I don't want it. I got better weapons.<end>
When did things turn south?<end>
I see where this is headed.<end>
You seriously didn't.<end>
Go on.<end>
I got this as my service pistol. <end>
To Nimble!<end>
To full bellies and full pockets!<end>
To loot!<end>
To peace!<end>
Did you think I'd leave you hanging?<end>
Wouldn't be mad even if you did. You didn't when it mattered.<end>
Root soda for me.<end>
Interesting. I'd never take you for a teetotaler.<end>
There is time.<end>
<end>
::She slides a glass of water toward you.::<end>
I quit recently.<end>
Doesn't mix with some other things I'm taking.<end>
I'm already drunk on adrenaline.<end>
Maybe it's time to stop. My life expectancy is already getting shorter and shorter.<end>
Actually, I'll have just a glass of water instead.<end>
::As soon as he sees you, he motions the girl::<end>
Have a good one, $(context.player.Name).<end>
<end>
I'll be at the Core City station in Upper Underrail.<end>

::After so many hours of darkness, the mood swiftly shifted the moment you stepped onto this stretch of gravel and steel, special for nothing else but the fact that it's underneath proper lights.
He takes a moment to absorb it all, then smiles.::
Finally.<end>
I second that.<end>
We didn't exactly reach North Underrail, but I'll take Upper Underrail over where Nimble and the rest went.<end>

::He readjusts his goggles.::
Now what?<end>
We make a good team. Maybe we should keep this up. Partner.<end>
We certainly do, but I think <end>
I've had enough excitement for the time being.<end>
What I need right now is a cold one, and some time to think things through.<end>
I could use some refreshment myself. And a proper conversation.<end>
Guess you earned it.<end>

Before I forget... ::He returns all of the items you gave him.:: Much obliged.
I'll be at that food stand at the Upper Underrail station in Core City. At least for a while.<end>
Must be at Zilla's. Got it.<end>
I'm sure I'll find you. Got it.<end>
::Nod and leave.::<end>
I'll consider it.<end>
I don't have time to be still. New experiences await.<end>
If you change your mind, <end>
I didn't come back empty-handed. I'm going straight to the merchants.<end>
Now we forget this sad adventure ever happened.<end>
I've gotten sick of dark territory myself.<end>
Uh, light.<end>
::You find him tweaking his energy pistol. Its compact screen is brightly reflected in his goggles.::<end>
<end>
A charon for your thoughts?<end>
Well, friend, there's some kind of electromagnetic interference here. ::He rechecks something on his pistol. Many lines of data scroll down its tiny display.::<end>

Don't know what it is, but it's affecting my equipment, and I'd bet more than that very charon you offered it's what's causing problems to the railcar, and by extension our poor friend Spanner here.<end>
Unusual weapon you got there. Never seen an energy pistol like that.<end>
It's a rare model. Can't find 'em anymore. Much like Torrence's.<end>
::[High-Technicalities]:: I only care about guns that shoot bright projectiles.<end>
Wouldn't wanna get shot with either.<end>
::He returns to his pistol. The screen flashes red a few times, but he changes the grip and everything reverts back to normal.::<end>
I gotta give it to the gunsmiths of old. They did know how to make them look good.<end>
Can't disagree with that. But for my line of work, I prefer this.<end>
We're like a traveling freak show, but the weapons are the freaks.<end>
Can't say you're wrong, but my opinion would've stayed the same even if you had cut that sentence a tad shorter.<end>
Where'd you get it?<end>
Had it for a long time...<end>
Mind if I ask you some questions?<end>
Now's not the time, friend.<end>
Don't forget where we are.<end>
I'll be leaving you to it.<end>
Much obliged.<end>
::Leave.::<end>
::He keeps his eyes on you, aided by a pair of seeker lenses.::<end>
<end>
Hate to sound rude, but I'm kind of invested in my lunch at the moment.<end>
::You see your very own reflection in his goggles.::<end>
